author: Christian Clason

relevant_verified_claims: Lipschitz derivative gives quadratic linearization remainder (Lemma 9.5).

TCC with eta<1 gives two-sided local comparison of nonlinear residual and derivative action (Theorem 9.8); with x†-x0 orthogonal to ker F'(x†), gives local uniqueness of x0-minimum-norm solution (Theorem 9.9).
Weak closedness and weakly closed domain yield nonlinear Tikhonov minimizer by direct method (Theorem 10.1); minimizer need not be unique, and stability is by weak cluster points (Theorem 10.2).
Variational source inequality with beta1<1 and alpha comparable to delta gives O(sqrt(delta)) solution error and O(delta) residual (Theorem 10.7).

Nonlinear Landweber under local TCC eta<1/2, derivative norm bound, local ball and Morozov threshold has Fejer monotonicity and finite stopping; exact/noisy convergence is established under the chapter's full assumptions (Theorems 11.3-11.6).

Nonlinear LM uses a Tikhonov-regularized linearized step; range approximation/forcing and stronger product-TCC assumptions yield a local discrepancy stopping bound O(1+|log delta|) (Theorems 11.8-11.13).
IRGNM with Lipschitz derivative, source smoothness nu in [1,2], small source norm, geometric alpha sequence and coupled stopping/noise condition gives O(delta^(nu/(nu+1))) (Theorems 11.15-11.16).
sources.limitations: Hilbert-space core; Banach methods, TV/sparsity, proximal methods and geometric constraints are outside the notes' main treatment. Statistical and Bayesian chapters are explicitly cursory.

sources.title: A note on convergence of solutions of total variation regularized linear inverse problems
author: José A. Iglesias
Gwenael Mercier
Otmar Scherzer
sources.extraction_coverage: All PDF pages extracted with PyMuPDF; page breaks retained.
sources.read_coverage: All pages 1-26, including appendices, figures and references, read.
relevant_verified_claims: For bounded linear A:L2(Omega)->L2(Sigma) in the stated 2D settings, the TV source condition is R(A*) intersect partial TV(u†) nonempty.

Fenchel duality identifies the TV dual feasible set; source condition is equivalent to limiting dual attainment; penalized dual maximizers converge strongly to the minimum-norm limiting certificate (Theorem 1, Lemma 2, Proposition 3).

AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-10-18: alpha_n -> 0 and ||w_n|| ||A*|| / alpha_n <= eta < 2 sqrt(pi) (full space/Dirichlet), or eta < 1/C(Omega) (Neumann); bounded Dirichlet domains require the variational-curvature lower-bound hypothesis. Subsequence, a.e.-level convergence in measure and Hausdorff convergence of boundaries to a selected minimum-TV limit (Theorem 2, PDF pp9-10, equations19-22).
sources.limitations: Linear forward map; spatial BV in 2D; particular full-space, Dirichlet and Neumann TV conventions. Does not prove a general nonlinear TV/Banach result.

sources.title: Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography
author: Barbara Kaltenbacher
sources.date: 2024-03-27; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis (2024), article drad044, online 2023
sources.extraction_coverage: All PDF pages extracted with PyMuPDF; page breaks retained.
sources.read_coverage: All pages 1-27, including appendix and references, read.
relevant_verified_claims: Differential range invariance can replace TCC when boundary/partial observation makes TCC unverifiable, but often requires relaxation and a penalty to restore the original parameter constraint (Sections 1-2).

Joint variational regularization with compatible VSC, index function, regularizer and tolerance/parameter coupling yields Bregman and residual rates (Theorem 3); split minimization requires additional hypotheses and a regularization correction (Theorem 5).
Frozen Newton rates require the explicit decreasing alpha, tolerance, stopping, conjugate-growth, beta-coupling, and small Taylor-remainder conditions (Theorem 7).

EIT examples verify range invariance and logarithmic variational-source rates under detailed 3D function-space and coefficient regularity assumptions (Sections 3, Theorems 8 and 10, Corollaries 9 and 11).
Without VSC, the appendix proves only subsequential convergence under explicit topology/compactness and parameter-scaling hypotheses; uniqueness upgrades this conclusion (Proposition 12).
sources.limitations: Banach formulation is present but applications and source conditions are tailored to PDE coefficient identification/EIT. The theorem hypotheses are extensive and cannot be generalized to arbitrary nonlinear maps or operator mismatch.

missing_proposed_prerequisites: Banach/Hilbert nonlinear forward operators, Fréchet derivative/adjoint, weak closedness and direct method
Tangential cone condition and differential range invariance, with valid residual comparison interfaces
Bregman distance, convex subdifferential, VSC, index functions and conjugate-rate calculus
Spatial BV, distributional gradients, finite perimeter, coarea, TV subgradient and domain boundary conventions
Nonlinear Tikhonov, nonlinear Landweber, regularized LM and IRGNM definitions and guarantee theorems with separate hypotheses
Sparse recovery nullspace/restricted injectivity/source-certificate prerequisites and manifold constraint geometry/compatibility prerequisites

limitations_of_lane_reading: No full sparsity/compressed-sensing textbook or paper was read; the report identifies conditions/modules to source during integration but does not claim support for a specific sparse recovery theorem.
No general manifold-valued inverse-problem source was read.
No spatial TV source was used to support nonlinear TV regularization; the complete TV paper covers linear maps only.
scope_attestation: Only planning evidence was added. No live content, item/page carriers, shared registries, build state, tests, gates, commits, or unrelated run files were modified.

audit_corrections.superseded_summary: With alpha=o(delta), source condition and boundary-specific assumptions, level sets converge in Hausdorff distance; proof uses curvature convergence and uniform density estimates for finite-perimeter sets (Theorem 2 and Section 4).
